articles.title: Prasidh Krishna injury concern clouds India's big win vs West Indies; Kotak confirms hamstring strain
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s emphatic eight-wicket win over West Indies in the second ODI came with an injury concern as fast bowler Prasidh Krishna suffered a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s emphatic eight-wicket win over West Indies in the second ODI came with an injury concern as fast bowler Prasidh Krishna suffered a hamstring strain and could bowl only five overs in Guwahati. India are monitoring the pacer’s condition, with scans scheduled to assess the extent of the injury on Thursday.Prasidh returned figures of 1/45 from his five overs after pulling up during his spell as West Indies posted a record 405/7. India subsequently chased down the target in just 43.3 overs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Prasidh being monitored, Dhir fineIndia batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed after the match that Prasidh was dealing with a hamstring strain and would undergo further assessment."Prasidh Krishna has a strain in the hamstring, he is being monitored. They will do scans and we will have an update by tomorrow evening," Kotak said.The injury could force India to make a change for the series finale in Mullanpur on Saturday. Prasidh is not part of the squad for the five-match T20I series against West Indies beginning in Lucknow on October 6.Naman Dhir also had to leave the field after twisting his ankle while bowling 6.1 overs, but Kotak played down concerns over the all-rounder, saying the issue was related to cramps."Naman is someone who normally doesn't get cramps, but it can happen," he said.Dhir had taken on an increased bowling workload after Prasidh's curtailed spell, while India’s other bowlers struggled to contain a West Indies batting line-up that piled up 405 runs.Kotak defends Guwahati pitch after record run-festThe injury concerns came after a remarkable batting-dominated contest in which more than 800 runs were scored and five centuries were recorded, including Shubman Gill’s double hundred and Rohit Sharma’s century.With the nature of the pitch drawing criticism, Kotak said there was no such thing as a perfect surface in cricket."When we talk about pitches, see, I don't think anyone in the world can make a so-called 'perfect pitch'," Kotak said."You can never say this wicket will have 250 or 300 runs. There will always be criticism (there is a batting collapse curators will be criticised and vice-versa when it turns out to be a belter)," he said.Kotak also pointed to the changing standards of ODI batting, noting how 183 was once a formidable total in the 60-over era before modern batting has pushed expectations towards 400-plus scores."So whether it is only the wicket to blame or the standard of batting is going high, the way guys are batting, it's debatable," he said."But yes, there will be a time when we'll have difficult wickets in one-day games also, and different venues will have different wickets. So hopefully by then we should be prepared."Rohit-Gill partnership leaves Kotak impressedKotak credited India’s top order for turning what initially appeared to be a daunting chase into a routine pursuit.Rohit and Gill added 255 for the opening wicket in only 26.2 overs before Virat Kohli contributed 29 off 19 balls. Gill remained unbeaten on 223 as India reached 406/2 in 43.3 overs."It's one of the best I have seen in ODI cricket," Kotak said of the Rohit-Gill partnership."It's one of the best I have seen in ODI cricket," he said about Rohit-Shubman's 255-run opening wicket stand that came in just 26.2 overs."The way we batted -- Shubman and Rohit started, and then Kohli also contributed. By 32 overs, 320 runs, the game was more or less over."Kotak also praised Gill’s hunger to convert his century into a huge score despite the heat and humidity."I feel players have that hunger. Normally we see a batter getting out after reaching hundred. But the way Gill was playing, I knew he would get a double," Kotak said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs, set up Asian Games gold-medal clash against Pakistan
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India produced a dominant all-round performance to crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the second men's cricket semifinal of the Asian Games in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India produced a dominant all-round performance to crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the second men's cricket semifinal of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Thursday, setting up a mouth-watering gold-medal clash against arch-rivals Pakistan on Saturday.After posting 169/7 on a turning pitch, India tore through Sri Lanka's batting line-up with a devastating new-ball burst and bowled them out for just 45 in 9.5 overs. The defending champions' bowlers never allowed Sri Lanka to settle into the chase, with Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma leading the rout.Pakistan had earlier booked their place in the final after beating Bangladesh by six wickets in the rain-truncated first semifinal.Scorecard: India vs Sri Lanka, Asian Games semifinalBumrah, Axar set up Sri Lanka collapseDefending 170, India made an explosive start as Bumrah struck twice in his opening over. A run-out in the second over added to Sri Lanka's problems, leaving them three wickets down almost immediately.Axar then tightened the screws in the fourth over, picking up two wickets to reduce Sri Lanka to 18/5. With the pitch offering considerable assistance to the spinners, the chase quickly turned into a procession.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleSri Lanka continued to lose wickets at regular intervals and had no answer to India's disciplined attack. Abhishek eventually completed the demolition job, taking two wickets in two balls to wrap up the innings at 45.The margin of victory underlined India's complete control of the semifinal and ensured the defending champions moved into Saturday's gold-medal match without having to face a serious challenge after the powerplay.Kishan, Sooryavanshi rescue IndiaIndia had also been tested with the bat after Sri Lanka opted to bowl first. The turning conditions made stroke-making difficult, and Sri Lanka used spin almost exclusively during the early part of the innings.Abhishek Sharma fell for seven after hitting a six, while Sanju Samson was dismissed for seven by ambidextrous spinner Tharindu Ratnayake.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, however, provided the spark India needed. The 15-year-old smashed 38 from just 21 balls, peppering the Sri Lankan attack with trademark strokeplay before falling to Sahan Arachchige.His innings included six fours and two sixes and helped India reach 58/2 in the powerplay. But wickets continued to fall, with captain Shreyas Iyer and Axar Patel also departing as Sri Lanka's spinners kept the pressure on.It was left to Ishan Kishan to provide the finishing push. The left-hander remained unbeaten on 80 from 46 balls, attacking the spinners down the ground and finding the boundary regularly. Four of his sixes came between long-on and long-off, while he also struck four fours.Kishan's composed assault ensured India reached a competitive 169/7, a total that proved more than enough once Bumrah and the spinners got to work.Pakistan await in gold-medal clashIndia's reward for the comprehensive victory is a high-profile final against Pakistan on Saturday. The two sides will now meet with the Asian Games gold medal at stake, adding another chapter to their long-running sporting rivalry.For India, the semifinal offered a reminder of their depth across both departments. Kishan and Sooryavanshi provided the impetus with the bat, while Bumrah's early strikes and Axar's double blow ensured Sri Lanka's chase never got going.The focus now shifts to the final, where India will look to complete their campaign with gold against Pakistan.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: MUMBAI: In a slight worry for India conjuring the busy cricket season ahead, it has emerged that fast bowler Prasidh Krishna will miss the third and final
articles.body: MUMBAI: In a slight worry for India conjuring the busy cricket season ahead, it has emerged that fast bowler Prasidh Krishna will miss the third and final ODI against West Indies, to be played at Mullanpur in Chandigarh on Saturday (October 3) due to a hamstring injury.Prasidh bowled only five overs (1-45) in India’s eight-wicket win in Guwahati before walking off the field. The Karnataka pacer has been diagnosed with a hamstring injury.Opening the attack, Prasidh bowled four overs initially. He returned for the 31st over for the second spell but it lasted for only one over and did not bowl again. Prasidh’s injury forced India to bowl part-timer Naman Dhir, who delivered 6.1 overs, although he too had earlier walked off the field due to a cramp.The Indian team is set to fly out of Guwahati on Thursday, but Prasidh will instead fly to Bengaluru and report to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, where he will undergo treatment for his injury.Prasidh is not part of the five-match T20I series that follows the ODIs and will begin in Lucknow on Oct 6, and thus he has some time to recover. However, considering the fine form that he has been in the last few months, India would hope that Prasidh recovers from the injury well in time before their upcoming tour of New Zealand, which starts with the opening T20I on Oct 22.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed after the match that Prasidh was dealing with a hamstring strain and would undergo further assessment."Prasidh Krishna has a strain in the hamstring, he is being monitored. They will do scans and we will have an update by tomorrow evening," Kotak said.Prasidh's absence could pave the way for Mohammed Siraj, who has been a bit controversially ‘rested’ from the first two ODIs, to play in the final ODI, though India also have the opinion of recalling allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, who was excluded from the second ODI.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Rishabh Pant had a disappointing outing in the Irani Cup as the Rest of India captain and wicketkeeper was dismissed for just 10 runs against Jammu & Kashmir at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium on Thursday.Pant, who faced 36 balls and hit one four, attempted to attack Umar Nazir but ended up slicing the ball straight to Qamran Iqbal at short cover-point. Pant stepped out of his crease and moved towards the leg side before trying to smash the delivery through the covers. However, he only managed to get a thick slice, bringing an end to his stay at the crease.Rest of India suffered another blow soon after Pant's dismissal when Saransh Jain was bowled by Sahil Lotra for 5. Lotra tossed the ball up and got it to dip and turn away, beating Jain's outside edge and crashing into the off stump.With Jain's dismissal, Rest of India slipped to 150/6 after 51 overs, having lost six wickets in the first innings. articles.title: Asian Games: India script history vs Sri Lanka, bowl out opposition for sub-50 total in T20Is for first time
articles.summary: India bowled Sri Lanka out for 45 in the Asian Games men's cricket semifinal in Nisshin, Japan, on Thursday.
articles.body: India bowled Sri Lanka out for 45 in the Asian Games men's cricket semifinal in Nisshin, Japan, on Thursday. The defending champions went on to win by 124 runs and set up a gold medal clash with Pakistan.Sri Lanka's 45 is also the joint-lowest T20I total by a Test-playing nation. West Indies were dismissed for the same score by England in 2019.The 45 all out was India's first time bowling an opposition side out for under 50 in T20Is. Their previous lowest total conceded was 57 for 10, scored by the United Arab Emirates in Dubai on September 10, 2025.Sri Lanka's collapse began in the powerplay, when they slipped to 31 for six while chasing India's 170-run target. Jasprit Bumrah struck twice in his opening over before Axar Patel also picked up two wickets.India needed only 9.5 overs to complete the win, with two run-outs adding to Sri Lanka's problems as the batters struggled on a turning track.Earlier, Ishan Kishan's calculated 46-ball 80 and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 38 off 21 balls helped India post 169 for seven in 20 overs after Sri Lanka won the toss and opted to bowl."We have to perform in both batting and bowling to win. We've been waiting for some days, there was a lot of rain around. To switch on and perform like this after a long break is commendable," Axar said after the match, referring to the washed-out quarterfinal against Afghanistan and the cancellation of practice sessions due to the weather in Japan.India's win also guaranteed them a medal in the men's cricket competition. They will face arch-rivals Pakistan in the gold medal match on Saturday.Sri Lanka will play Bangladesh in the bronze medal match. Bangladesh had lost to Pakistan earlier in the day.Both the bronze medal match and the final will be played on Saturday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia cricket team: Batter Nic Maddinson recalled after testicular cancer recovery
articles.summary: Australia recall Nic Maddinson for the first Test against South Africa after the New South Wales batter recovered from testicular cancer.
articles.body:
Australia have recalled Nic Maddinson for the first Test against South Africa after the New South Wales batter recovered from testicular cancer.

Maddinson and uncapped Victoria wicketkeeper Sam Harper have been added to the touring squad as cover for Josh Inglis, who will miss the series opener with a finger injury.

The 34-year-old Maddinson, who played three Tests for Australia in late 2016, was diagnosed with testicular cancer, which spread to his lung and lymph nodes, in April 2025.

He completed a course of chemotherapy in July 2025 and was given the all-clear to resume his career eight weeks after his final round of treatment.

He has not played first-class cricket since his diagnosis, but he made five appearances in last season's Big Bash League and scored 126 for New South Wales against Victoria on Sunday in Australia's domestic one-day competition.

Harper, 29, made 128 for Australia A against India A in the ongoing unofficial Test in Puducherry this week and scored 677 runs in the 2025-26 Sheffield Shield season.

Maddinson and Harper come into contention for selection for the first game in the three-match series, which starts in Durban on Friday, 9 October.

"Sam give us wicketkeeping cover as Josh continues his recovery while Nic provides flexibility throughout the batting order," said Australia chair of selectors George Bailey.

All-rounder Cameron Green is a doubt for the first Test, after he sustained a lower abdominal strain while batting in the last of the three ODIs that preceded the red-ball series.

In the case of Inglis, initial scans confirmed a fracture of his right index finger, with the injury to be monitored before a possible return for the second Test in Gqeberha.

articles.title: 2027 Cricket World Cup draw: England avoid Australia & India in group stage
articles.summary: England avoid defending champions Australia and world number one-ranked side India in the group-stage draw for the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.
articles.body:
England have avoided defending champions Australia and world number one-ranked side India in the group-stage draw for the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup.

India and Pakistan are, once again, placed in the same group, alongside Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier.

England, who won the trophy in 2019, are in the same group as co-hosts South Africa, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, New Zealand and a qualifier.

Harry Brook's side, who have enjoyed a resurgence in the 50-over format, begin their campaign against Bangladesh on 8 October, and Sri Lanka on 13 October in Windhoek, Namibia.

They will come up against South Africa in Gqeberha on 16 October before travelling to Harare to face a qualifier on 20 October. They round off the group stage when they face New Zealand, again in Gqeberha, on 23 October.

The visit to Zimbabwe is significant, with England having not played there since 2004.

Political unrest in Zimbabwe under the regime of former president Robert Mugabe caused problems for England's men's team throughout the 2000s.

England boycotted their fixture against Zimbabwe in Harare at the 2003 World Cup - a decision which ultimately derailed their campaign.

Relations have improved in recent years, however, and BBC Sport reported in 2025 that the two cricket boards were discussing a potential England tour of the country in the next cycle of international cricket between 2027 and 2031.

After three matches to decide the final two qualifiers, the tournament group stage will open with a repeat of the 2023 final when India and Australia face each other in Cape Town on 7 October.

Arch-rivals India and Pakistan, who do not play each other outside tournaments, will meet in Johannesburg on 10 October.

The top three, plus the best fourth-placed finisher, from the two groups progress to the Super 7 stage.

From there, the top four teams will qualify for the semi-finals, which are scheduled for 17 and 18 November, before the final on 21 November in Johannesburg.

articles.summary: Afghanistan pacer Fazalhaq Farooqi became the most expensive player in International League T20 (ILT20) Player Auction history after being bought by MI
articles.body: Afghanistan pacer Fazalhaq Farooqi became the most expensive player in International League T20 (ILT20) Player Auction history after being bought by MI Emirates for USD 380,000 on Thursday.Farooqi will join MI Emirates for a fifth consecutive season. His deal broke the auction record for the third time during the day.Liam Livingstone had earlier set a new record when Gulf Giants bought him for USD 350,000. Before Livingstone, Gulf Giants had used their Right-to-Match option to retain Afghanistan batter Rahmanullah Gurbaz for USD 310,000, making him the most expensive player in ILT20 auction history at that point.Before Gurbaz, Faf du Plessis held the record after joining Dubai Capitals for USD 300,000.Babar Azam was bought by Desert Vipers for his base price of USD 80,000. It will be his first season in the ILT20.Moreover, West Indies pacer Alzarri Joseph was also snapped by Gulf Giants for $230,000. Allah Ghazanfar was another notable signing, joining for USD 150,000, while Mohammad Nabi was bought for USD 140,000 and Dasun Shanaka for USD 100,000.The Season 5 Player Auction was held in Dubai on Thursday, October 1, with more than 200 players from 23 countries in the auction pool. The list included Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Tom Banton, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Wanindu Hasaranga, Alzarri Joseph, Faf du Plessis and Liam Livingstone.The six franchises entered the auction with purses ranging from $1.3 million to $1.39 million and built squads of between 18 and 23 players. articles.title: ‘Where is the contest between bat and ball?’ 811-run IND vs WI Guwahati ODI raises questions
articles.summary: KOCHI: 811 runs were scored in 93.3 overs in the second ODI between India and West Indies at Guwahati on a ridiculous day of batting, when bowlers were
articles.body: KOCHI: 811 runs were scored in 93.3 overs in the second ODI between India and West Indies at Guwahati on a ridiculous day of batting, when bowlers were reduced to mute spectators. Once, a match like this would have been celebrated like a historic event. Now, it’s just another game of cricket. A game like this doesn’t thrill the audience; it leaves them weary of watching another run-fest on a pitch described as a ‘national highway’ by Ravi Shastri on commentary.India captain Shubman Gill’s unbeaten 223 was sublime, his impeccable timing, placement and voracious appetite hallmarks of his talent. So too was Rohit Sharma’s easy-on-the-eye 101. The West Indies also had three centurions. These batters needed adversaries, and they found none. Not from the bowlers nor from the pitch.“Extremely boring game yaar,” Madan Lal, former medium-pacer and member of India’s 1983 World Cup-winning squad, told TOI.“Over 800 runs scored on a paata wicket and there was absolutely nothing in it for the bowlers. Give the bowlers something to play with. Where is the contest between bat and ball?" Lal observed.He reckons that an ideal ODI should end around 280 per side. The kind of game that offers a genuine contest and the one that spectators want to watch. For that to happen, he says the curators must put some life into these insipid wickets. “I don’t think that will happen,” he laments.Former Delhi pacer Sanjiv Sharma attributes the trend to the proliferation of T20Is and expects more teams to chase down 400+ scores in ODIs going forward.“In T20Is, we see teams chase down 200+ scores. Batters are carrying that confidence into the 50-over format,” he said.Lal points out that the real worry about such run-fests is that in the long term it kills the quality of bowling. Sharma concurred. “Apart from Kuldeep (Yadav), neither side had a match-winner with the ball. India had a second-string attack, but what about the West Indies? Their bowling was abysmal,” he added.One-day cricket is in an existential crisis in a calendar surfeit with T20Is. The lure of the 50-over game is that, unlike the T20Is, it gives time for a contest to build, turn and breathe. Gill’s second double hundred in this format will find its way into the record books, but a record without contest is mere arithmetic.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 2027 Cricket World Cup: England avoid Australia and India in group stage as fixtures revealed for 50-over tournament
articles.summary: England drawn alongside South Africa, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and qualifier for pool phase of event that runs from October 2 to November 21, 2027; World Cup final will be held at Wanderers in Johannesburg, the same venue for the India vs Pakistan match on October 10
articles.body:
Harry Brook's side are placed in Group B alongside New Zealand, co-hosts South Africa, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and a qualifier for a tournament that runs from October 2 to November 21 next year.

Defending champions Australia join India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, another co-host Zimbabwe and a qualifier in Group A of the event.

Namibia will also host matches during the tournament.

Australia face India in a repeat of the 2023 final - which the Baggy Greens won by six wickets in Ahmedabad to claim a record-extending sixth title - in the group-stage opener in Cape Town on October 7.

That game will be preceded by three qualifying matches, on October 2, 4, and 6, to determine the final entrant for the competition proper.

England, champions on home soil in 2019 before being dumped out in round one in India four years later, begin their campaign against Bangladesh in Windhoek, Namibia on October 8, while they then face Sri Lanka at the same venue on October 13.

A meeting with South Africa follows in Gqeberha on October 16, ahead of a game against a qualifier in Harare on October 20.

England then return to Gqeberha on October 23 to conclude the group stage campaign against New Zealand, the side they edged on boundary countback to win the 2019 final at Lord's and claim a maiden ODI World Cup title.

In Group A, India face Pakistan in Johannesburg on October 10.

Those two nations only face each other in major tournaments due to political unrest.

The top three teams in each pool plus the best fourth-placed side will advance to the Super 7 stage, with the top four countries after that phase making the semi-finals on November 17 and 18, in Cape Town and Centurion respectively.

The final will take place in Johannesburg on November 21.

articles.title: Johannesburg to host Cricket World Cup final and India vs. Pakistan game in 2027 edition
articles.summary: Johannesburg will host the final of next year's Cricket World Cup as well as a marquee game between archrivals Pakistan and India.  The International Cricket...
articles.body:
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — Johannesburg will host the final of next year's Cricket World Cup as well as a marquee game between archrivals Pakistan and India.

The International Cricket Council on Thursday announced the schedule of the 2027 edition of the tournament. A total of 12 venues will host matches across three countries: South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe.

The India-Pakistan match is scheduled for Oct. 10 in Johannesburg, which also will host the Nov. 21 final.

The 12 nations are split into two groups with defending champion Australia, India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier in Group A. New Zealand, South Africa, Sri Lanka, England, Bangladesh and another qualifier are placed in Group B.

The two qualifiers will be confirmed after a 10-team tournament early next year. The winner will advance to the group stage of the mega event. The losing finalist and the two losing semifinalists will play the Super Series at Namibia ahead of the World Cup with the winner advancing as the second qualifier.

The group stage of the tournament begins at Cape Town on Oct. 7 when Australia takes on India in a repeat of 2023 World Cup final. Newlands in Capetown, which has an iconic mountain backdrop, will also host a semifinal on Nov. 17. The second semifinal on Nov. 18 will be played at Centurion's SuperSport Park.

The ICC said that top 10 teams on its rankings to Sept. 30 this year have gained automatic qualification. Zimbabwe, the co-host of the tournament, begins its campaign on Oct. 11 with a game against Afghanistan at Bulawayo.

"South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia will provide an unforgettable stage for the world's best teams, combining a deep passion for cricket, extraordinary destinations and a renowned warmth of welcome," ICC chairman Jay Shah said in a statement.

After the group stage, the top three teams from both groups advance to the Super 7 stage. The seventh team will be the best fourth-place side across the two groups.

The ICC said to provide clarity for fans, teams and stakeholders, a number of teams have been pre-seeded into designated Super 7 stage, no matter where it finishes among the top three during the group stage like, India and New Zealand are A1 and B1 respectively in their groups.

England will play two group games in Namibia while a newly built Victoria Falls ground in Zimbabwe hosts the final game of the group stage between the co-host and India on Oct. 24. An additional three games in Super 7 stage will also be hosted at the same venue.

The top four teams after the Super 7 phase advance to the semifinals. Top finisher will play against the fourth place team with the second and third-placed teams going head-to-head in the other semi-final.

articles.title: Simi Singh: An Ireland dream, a life-threatening detour and the journey home
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Simranjit Singh, known as Simi Singh in Ireland and across world cricket, had already retired in his mind when acute liver failure brought his
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Simranjit Singh, known as Simi Singh in Ireland and across world cricket, had already retired in his mind when acute liver failure brought his career to a shuddering halt in 2024. But on Wednesday, he closed the chapter officially, announcing his retirement and bringing down the curtain on a remarkable 20-year association with Ireland, the country he moved to in 2006 to pursue hotel management, only to find a second life in cricket.Over his two decades in Ireland, the highs were incredibly high, but the lows were devastating as well.“I played international cricket, represented Ireland in the World Cup (T20), scored a century while batting at No. 8 against South Africa in ODIs and picked up a five-wicket haul as well. Recently, I came to know that I have the best economy rate in ODIs (3.99), with Rashid Khan second. When I packed my bags and left for Ireland as a teenager, playing cricket was not something I had in my mind. It was special,” Simi told TimesofIndia.com.“The people at Cricket Ireland were not surprised because, even before this, I was not being considered for selection. It had become difficult to play professional cricket, especially with my recovery still going on. So I thought it was better to properly close things and make an official announcement so that everyone knew,” added Simi, who played 35 ODIs and 53 T20Is for Ireland.In early 2024, Simi’s life was turned upside down after he developed a mysterious fever. Doctors in Ireland were unable to find the underlying cause and his health began to deteriorate. He eventually moved to India in search of better medical opinions, only to discover that he had developed acute liver failure. His wife, Agamdeep Kaur, donated part of her liver to save his life.“My wife is my guardian angel. She was God-sent. She gave me a new life. It was a torrid time for the family,” he said.“Now I have moved back to Mohali. Recovery is still going on. There is improvement, but it is slow. I will survive,” he added.It was never all hunky-dory for Simi in Ireland. With tough residency rules, his ECB Level 2 coaching qualification and certification as a personal trainer helped him stay afloat before he eventually broke into the national team. Now, the coaching qualification he earned all those years ago has come to the fore. He has opened his own cricket academy in Mohali, the city where he toiled during his formative years and represented Punjab successfully at the U-14 and U-17 levels.“For now, I am not running the academy myself. I have completed Level 2 with the England Cricket Board, and I am thinking of doing Level 3. Then we will see what opportunities come up,” he said.When Simi left India in 2006, he was frustrated that his cricketing career had failed to take off. Nearly two decades later, the 39-year-old looks back at his journey with a sense of gratitude — or shukrana, as he puts it in Punjabi.“I am relaxed here. My parents are fine. My dad even came to the ground with me. It is good to be back home. My parents were getting old. I am not missing any festivals. Now the coming and going and all that headache is over,” he said.For someone who left India as a teenager without cricket even figuring in his plans, Simi’s journey has come full circle. Ireland gave him a career he had stopped believing was possible. Then he fought a life-threatening illness but his wife gave him a second chance at life. Now, with cricket behind him as a player, Simi wants to build the next chapter from Mohali, closer to home and with a renewed sense of gratitude.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: New Delhi: India will begin their 2027 ODI World Cup campaign against defending champions Australia in Cape Town on October 7, the International Cricket
articles.body: New Delhi: India will begin their 2027 ODI World Cup campaign against defending champions Australia in Cape Town on October 7, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced in Cape Town on Thursday.The two finalists from the last edition will kick off the round-robin stage. The tournament will begin on October 2 with a three-match Super Series to determine two qualifiers.As has been the trend in ICC events over the last decade, India and Pakistan have been drawn in the same group and are slated to face each other on October 10 in Johannesburg. The 51-day tournament will conclude with the final in Johannesburg on November 21.India will get a two-day break before the match against Pakistan, who will play their opening match against Afghanistan in Tshwane on October 8.The 12 teams have been divided into two groups, with the top three from each group and the best fourth-placed team advancing to the Super 7 phase, followed by the two semifinals.Besides India, Australia and Pakistan, the other teams in Group A are Afghanistan and Zimbabwe, with one qualifier yet to be decided.Interestingly, the seedings for the Super 7 phase have been pre-decided on the basis of the ICC ODI rankings as of September 30, 2026. India, Australia and Pakistan are seeded A1, A2 and A3 respectively, while England are seeded AB4. New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka are seeded B1, B2 and B3 respectively.Should a non-seeded team finish in a qualifying position above a pre-seeded team, it will assume the Super 7 position allocated to the pre-seeded team it has displaced.This has been done to make it easier for fans to plan their travel for the tournament.Group B features hosts South Africa, England, New Zealand, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, along with the other qualifier.The Super 7 seedings will remain fixed irrespective of where the top three teams from each group finish in the first round. articles.body: On a gripping opening day of the Irani Cup at Srinagar’s Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium, honours were shared between Rest of India and Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir, with 12 wickets falling on a seam-friendly surface.Karnataka’s rising star Ravichandran Smaran once again underlined his batting promise with a rescue act. With Rest of India reeling at 155 for seven after being sent in to bat, the 23-year-old left-hander produced a composed 68 off 83 balls, with eight fours and a six, to steer his side to a respectable 237 in 68.1 overs.Batting at No. 6, Smaran found valuable support from Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan, who struck a fluent 60 off 118 balls, including nine fours and a six. Their efforts ensured Rest of India recovered from a position of serious trouble against an inspired J&K pace attack.In the absence of spearhead Auqib Nabi, J&K’s seamers Sunil Kumar (3-26) and Lone Nasir Muzaffar (3-59) shared six wickets, while Umar Nazir marked his return after nearly a year out with injury with figures of 2-65.Their disciplined effort kept the visitors under pressure throughout the day.J&K then lost two early wickets in their reply to finish on 21 for two after seven overs.Brief scores: Rest of India (1st innings) 237 in 68.1 overs (Ravichandran Smaran 68, Shikhar Mohan 60; Sunil Kumar 3/36, Lone Nasir Muzaffar 3/59); Jammu & Kashmir 21/2 in 7 overs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘She would  be sitting on the bench again’: Gujarat Giants explain Danni Wyatt-Hodge release
articles.summary: Mumbai: Gujarat Giants retained a large chunk of their squad ahead of the 2027 Women's Premier League player auction, a departure from the second season
articles.body: Mumbai: Gujarat Giants retained a large chunk of their squad ahead of the 2027 Women's Premier League player auction, a departure from the second season when they released 11 players. But they surprised by letting go of England batter Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who finished as the top run-scorer in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup in England.Wyatt-Hodge scored 302 runs in seven matches at 60.40, including a century and two fifties, at a strike rate of 149.50, helping England reach the final.Gujarat Giants head coach Michael Klinger said Wyatt-Hodge was released because she was likely to spend much of WPL 2027 on the bench, with England also having commitments during the tournament."As you would have seen last year, she didn't quite fit into our four overseas lineup for the majority of the time. I felt for her. She came in for one game and started reasonably well, getting about 12 or 15. Then she got sick just before the next game and was left out. Georgia Wareham came back in and had a really good game, and we stuck with that middle order all round option."This year, England have commitments during the WPL. If we went with a similar setup, she would probably be sitting on the bench again. I spoke to both her and her representative, and they are keen for her to play some cricket during that time, leading into the Champions Trophy. I'm not sure whether she will enter the auction, but she was quite keen to play that England series around the same time. So for both parties, this was the best way to go. It also gives us another option in the auction, either the same skill set or a different one," Klinger said at an interaction on Thursday.Titas releaseKlinger said injury concerns also contributed to the decision to release India pacer Titas Sadhu, who has played 20 white-ball internationals."What probably went against her this time was her injuries. She had an injury last season where we didn't really get a chance to see her, and she has been injured since. She is just making her comeback now."We are having a training camp at the moment and we still asked her to come so we could have a look at her before the auction. She is progressing well and will start the domestic season on the 26th of October. Releasing her gives us a few more options in the auction. There is no reason we may not look to get her back, but it also gives us a chance to look at other options," he said.Fast-bowling depthKlinger believes India's domestic fast-bowling pool has improved, though the real test will come against international batters.“Overall, domestically, I think fast bowling is the area where Indian cricket can keep building depth. There has been a big change from when I started in this role a few years ago. The fast bowlers around the country are physically better. When you watch them bowl and field, they are fitter, more versatile, move better and are more agile."That is only going to help them maintain pace and aggression for longer periods without injury. So I think Indian cricket is definitely on the right track in building depth in fast bowling. The test is always when they come up against international batters, whether that's international Indian batters or overseas batters in the WPL, because a lot of these bowlers haven't done that before. That's always the biggest test when they get on the big stage,” Klinger said.Giants target bowling consistencyAfter missing the playoffs in their first two seasons, Gujarat Giants have reached the knockout stage in the last two. Klinger, who is overseeing an off-season camp in Bengaluru ahead of the October 28 auction in Kochi, identified bowling consistency as an area for improvement."To be honest, we just had a bad final against Delhi Capitals. We beat them twice during the season in close games and didn't bring our best in that eliminator. That was disappointing, because I felt we probably had a stronger season than DC did throughout the year. But that's what finals are about. You need your best players to step up, and we probably didn't.""I think we can get more consistency with our bowling. Looking at the data and statistical information from last season, that's one area where we can improve. We have the personnel, and a couple of players are putting their hand up to get opportunities there this year, which will help us get some more quality overs."Last year we defended some really big scores, but they were pretty tight games, and we also chased some big scores. I feel our batting is strong. If we can tighten up our bowling at certain times, then we'll be fine," he added.Anushka, Happy in focusKlinger backed Anushka Sharma after her impressive first WPL season and said her experience of international cricket could provide extra motivation."Anushka Sharma was fantastic for us last year in her first WPL season. She has had a really good ODI series against Australia A and had a taste of international cricket. She probably could have been kept a little longer with more opportunities there, but I'm hoping that works in our favour."Having tasted international cricket, I'm sure she will be desperate to do everything she can to get back. Both she and Yastika (Bhatia, who too will play for GG in WPL-2027) are in the same boat, playing for India at the moment. I'm hoping they will have a lot of motivation to have a really good WPL and help break back into the Indian starting 11. That gives them great motivation, which can only help us as well."Klinger also identified young fast bowler Happy Kumari as a player to watch."One other I would mention, though it's hard to pinpoint because we have great skill sets throughout the squad, is Happy Kumari, a young fast bowler. We saw her progress and train really well for us last year. She got one opportunity in a match and has been working hard since. If she keeps progressing that way, she may get more games for us in this WPL. I'm looking forward to seeing her keep improving up until January," he concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'You feel bad': Rishabh Pant breaks silence on losing India ODI spot to KL Rahul
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant's Test legacy continues to grow, but his standing in India's white-ball plans has become increasingly uncertain.
articles.body: Rishabh Pant's Test legacy continues to grow, but his standing in India's white-ball plans has become increasingly uncertain. More than two years have passed since he last featured in an ODI for India, leaving his 50-over future unclear.Pant has played considerably fewer ODIs than Tests and T20Is. In 31 ODI appearances, he has scored 871 runs at an average of 33.50, with his best being an unbeaten 125 against England in 2022. It remains his only hundred in the format, alongside five fifties.When India announced their squad for the West Indies ODI series, Pant was once again left out. Being named captain of the Rest of India side for the Irani Cup would have offered little consolation to a player still hoping to return to India's 50-over set-up.Pant admitted that being dropped hurts, but said setbacks are part of an athlete's journey.“Definitely, you feel bad when something like this happens. But an athlete’s mindset allows you to feel that when there’s a setback, there is always a comeback. These are things that, as an athlete, you have to deal with in your day-to-day life. People say this happened to me, that happened to me, but for an athlete, this is part and parcel of the game. But at the same time, you know how hard you’re working, and you’re clear in your path to maintain at this level,” Pant said on the Business of Sport podcast.“To make it happen every day, there is a voice in your head that is very constant in a very disciplined manner. The only thing is it’s easier to pass opinions all the time, but at the same time, people have to wait for things to happen.”Pant's absence from the 2023 World Cup followed the accident that kept him out of professional cricket for a year. In his absence, KL Rahul established himself as India's primary wicketkeeper-batter in ODIs.The competition for the wicketkeeper's slot has only grown. Ishan Kishan, despite holding the record for the fastest ODI double century, has not established himself as an integral part of India's 50-over side, while Dhruv Jurel is also part of the squad for the West Indies ODIs.Pant's T20I prospects have also become less certain. Sanju Samson is India's primary wicketkeeper in the format and was named Player of the Tournament at the T20 World Cup, while Ishan has also taken up the wicketkeeping role when Samson has not been in the playing XI.Pant has also not made a particularly strong case with the bat in his last two IPL seasons. In IPL 2025, he scored 269 runs at an average of 24.45 and a strike rate of 133.17, with his campaign including a century in the final league game. In the following season, he made 312 runs at an average of 28.36 and a strike rate of 138.Pant, however, remains determined to force his way back.“There is no doubt that I have to make it happen, because for me, I feel like I haven’t had the best of opportunities to give my best, but at the same time, international cricket is changing. Sometimes you have to wait for the chance and make things happen,” Pant added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Unfinished business’: Shubman Gill eyes 2027 ODI World Cup redemption, values Virat Kohli-Rohit Sharma experience
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill has already started looking towards the 2027 ODI World Cup, and for India's captain, the tournament represents more than another
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill has already started looking towards the 2027 ODI World Cup, and for India's captain, the tournament represents more than another opportunity on the global stage. It is unfinished business.Gill, the world's No. 1-ranked ODI batter, reflected on India's heartbreaking end to the 2023 World Cup campaign and the significance of getting another chance to compete for the biggest prize in ODI cricket. Speaking to JioStar ahead of the third ODI against the West Indies, Gill also underlined the value of having two vastly experienced campaigners — Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma — around him as he grows into his leadership role.India had gone through the 2023 World Cup unbeaten in the league stage and entered the final against Australia as the tournament's standout side before suffering a six-wicket defeat in Ahmedabad.For Gill, that painful ending still carries significance.‘It is unfinished business’"Yes, absolutely, it's unfinished business because of the way we played throughout that World Cup. We were looking like the best team in the tournament. But World Cups are like that. You might play the entire tournament well, but you don't play one game well, and that game could be the final of the World Cup," Gill told JioStar.The India captain also highlighted how limited the opportunities are for a player to compete in a World Cup, making every appearance particularly precious."So definitely, it is unfinished business. And as a player, you don't get that many opportunities to represent your country in a World Cup. There could be two, three, four, five, you never know. So, every World Cup that you play for your country is a big honour. So, very grateful to be able to play another one."The 2027 edition will therefore carry an added significance for a young India side that will enter the tournament with Gill at the helm and a mix of emerging players and established stars.‘Extremely lucky’ to have Virat and RohitWhile Gill is increasingly assuming responsibility as captain, he is also benefiting from the presence of two of India's most experienced ODI players.Kohli and Rohit remain important figures in the dressing room, and Gill believes their experience can be invaluable as India prepare for another World Cup campaign."I feel extremely lucky. Virat bhai is probably the best ODI batter, and Rohit bhai is the best ODI opener in the world. And then to be able to have these two players in the team and their experience, and the moments that they have shared together, it's great, and we really enjoy having them in the team. And their experience is very valuable for us," he said.For Gill, learning from senior players is not restricted to Kohli and Rohit. He also seeks the views of other experienced members of the squad before making decisions on the field."Often, not just those two; I go to even KL or Shreyas, for that matter. I like to take everyone's opinion," Gill said.He explained that captaincy, for him, involves listening to different perspectives before deciding what he believes will work best in a particular situation."But most of the time, it happens that if they come to suggest something, then I might have thought about it. If I haven't thought about it, then I'll think about what their thoughts are, what their opinions are. So, you listen to everyone, see what they are thinking, and then what, according to me, would work best in that situation; I think learning comes from that."No. 1 ranking takes a back seatGill's own evolution has been rapid. He is currently the No. 1-ranked ODI batter, a position he first reached during the 2023 World Cup.While becoming the world's top-ranked ODI batter was once a personal ambition, Gill now places greater emphasis on what his performances contribute to the team."The first time when I became the number one-ranked batsman, I think it was during the 2023 World Cup. And it felt good. As a kid, you look at the rankings, so it was like a tick mark that, 'Okay, once I want to become the number one-ranked ODI batsman.' So it feels good, but I think right now it doesn't matter as much. For me, it's more important that if you step out in a match, go to bat, then how you can make the team win, how you can contribute," he said.That shift in perspective is also reflected in how Gill views captaincy. Rather than treating the role as a burden, he sees it as a responsibility entrusted to him."I look at it more like a responsibility. Even while growing up, it was not really my dream that I had to become India's captain one day. My dream was always to play for the country and win matches for my country, and that was always my aim growing up," he said."So, when I got this opportunity to captain, obviously, it was a big honour and a big responsibility. And I look at it as I have been given the responsibility of the team, and that makes things a lot easier for me. I don't feel that much pressure about this thing because I feel that if I do things with the right intent, then everything will fall into place."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs Pakistan final: What happens if rain washes out Asian Games gold medal clash?
articles.summary: India and Pakistan are set to battle for the men's cricket gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games, but persistent rain in Nisshin could throw a major twist
articles.body: India and Pakistan are set to battle for the men's cricket gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games, but persistent rain in Nisshin could throw a major twist into Saturday's summit clash.India booked their place in the final with a commanding 124-run win over Sri Lanka in the semi-final. After being asked to bat, Shreyas Iyer's side posted 169/7 in 20 overs before Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma claimed two wickets each to bowl Sri Lanka out for just 45.The victory guaranteed India at least a silver medal, but the team will now be hoping the weather does not prevent them from competing for gold against arch-rivals Pakistan.What happens if rain washes out India vs Pakistan final?The weather forecast in Nisshin could be a concern. According to AccuWeather, there is a 62% chance of rain in the morning on Saturday, with the probability expected to fall to 25% in the afternoon. The temperature is likely to remain around 20 degrees Celsius, while cloud cover is expected to be about 37%.If rain prevents the final from producing a result, the rules for the 2026 Asian Games are different from those used at the previous edition.At the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, India's men's team won the gold medal after the final against Afghanistan was washed out. India were declared champions because they were the higher-ranked T20I side.That rule does not apply in Nisshin.Under the regulations for the ongoing edition, if the final is abandoned without a result, the gold medal will be shared by India and Pakistan. Both finalists would therefore be declared joint gold medallists.India enter final after dominant semi-finalIndia's route to the final was emphatic. Iyer and Co. recovered to post 169/7 after being sent in by Sri Lanka, with Ishan Kishan playing a key role in the innings.The bowlers then made short work of the Sri Lankan chase. Bumrah, Axar and Abhishek picked up two wickets apiece as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 45, giving India a 124-run victory.Pakistan also reached the final after winning their semi-final, setting up the first meeting between the two sides in the men's cricket competition at the Asian Games.For India, the stakes are particularly significant. They are the defending champions and have brought a full-strength team to Japan, including pace spearhead Bumrah. A victory would allow them to retain the gold medal they won at Hangzhou.But if the rain has the final say and no result is possible, neither side will take gold outright. The 2026 Asian Games rules mean India and Pakistan will share the gold medal.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I am not done yet': Yuzvendra Chahal announces retirement from first-class cricket
articles.summary: India leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal on Friday announced his retirement from first-class cricket, bringing an end to his red-ball career after 17 years.
articles.body: India leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal on Friday announced his retirement from first-class cricket, bringing an end to his red-ball career after 17 years.Chahal said his dream of playing Test cricket may not be fulfilled, but he remains determined to continue playing white-ball cricket for India.The 35-year-old, who has played 72 ODIs and 80 T20Is for India, never got the chance to play a Test match. His last international appearance came in a T20I against the West Indies in August 2023.148 wickets in first-class cricketChahal made his first-class debut for Haryana in 2009. He finished his red-ball career with 148 wickets from 49 matches at an average of 32.27. He played his last first-class match at Lord's and said the Test cap remained a dream throughout his career.Announcing his decision on Instagram, Chahal looked back at his journey with the red ball."The first cricket ball I ever held was a red ball. I was 10 years old, and I had no idea then how deeply I would fall in love with this game."For me, red-ball cricket was never just another format. It was where I learned the meaning of patience, character, resilience and the pure joy of being out there for hours, fighting for every run and every wicket."I played my last First-Class match at Lords, saying these words is emotional as a Test cap was always a dream, one that I carried with me for many years. It may not have happened, but I am genuinely content with the journey I have had and incredibly grateful for every opportunity that came my way in this format."The red ball gave me some of the most beautiful memories of my life, and nothing will ever take that away."'I AM NOT DONE YET'While Chahal has walked away from first-class cricket, he made it clear that he has no plans to stop playing international cricket."But I AM NOT DONE YET. The hunger to play for my country is still very much alive. I believe I have the cricket left in me, and I will give everything I have to earn another opportunity in the One-Day and T20 formats," he said.Chahal also thanked the Haryana Cricket Association and its former officials for their support throughout his career."A special thank you to the Haryana Cricket Association, Mr. Ranbir Singh Mahindra Sir and Mr. Anirudh Singh Chaudhary Sir for their continuous support, trust and belief throughout my journey. From a 10-year-old holding his first red ball to playing his final First-Class game, it has been one hell of a journey," Chahal said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Former India opener Aakash Chopra has predicted that Virat Kohli will finish his international career with 98 centuries.In a video posted by Cricinfo on X, Chopra was asked how many centuries Kohli would have by the time he retires. He replied 98. Kohli, who only plays ODI now, currently has 86 international centuries and needs 15 more to surpass Sachin Tendulkar’s record of 100 international hundreds.Tendulkar played 664 international matches across formats between 1989 and 2013. He scored 100 centuries, including 51 in 200 Tests and 49 in 463 ODIs.Kohli, meanwhile, has scored 55 centuries in ODIs, 30 in Tests and one in T20Is.Chopra was also asked to name India’s best white-ball fast bowler apart from Jasprit Bumrah. He picked Arshdeep Singh.Arshdeep is India’s leading wicket-taker in T20Is, with 140 wickets from 94 matches. However, he has played only 18 ODIs since making his debut against New Zealand in November 2022.Arshdeep is also not a guaranteed pick in India’s ODI team for the 2027 World Cup.When asked about the biggest question mark in India’s ODI team, Chopra identified two areas of concern and said, “What happens if Hardik is unfit?"Hardik Pandya is an important part of India’s white-ball teams but has not played competitive cricket since the end of IPL 2026. His last appearance for India came against New Zealand in the final of the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026 on March 8 in Ahmedabad.India will face West Indies in the third and final ODI of the ongoing series at the New Chandigarh Stadium on Saturday. articles.title: IPL retentions: 'Unhappy' Abhishek Sharma wants to leave SRH but where will he go?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian Premier League (IPL) retentions and releases discussions are underway across franchises as the deadline approaches, with Sunrisers
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian Premier League (IPL) retentions and releases discussions are underway across franchises as the deadline approaches, with Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) opener Abhishek Sharma emerging as the biggest talking point. With the franchise keen to hand the captaincy to Ishan Kishan, and Pat Cummins likely to remain unavailable due to an intense international calendar in 2027, the belligerent opener is understood to be exploring a new home as early as the upcoming season.TimesofIndia.com can confirm that there has been informal dialogue with multiple franchises, but nothing substantial has materialised yet. Mumbai Indians (MI), Gujarat Titans (GT) and Punjab Kings (PBKS) are the teams being mentioned as potential destinations, but a well-placed industry source asserts that it's a tricky situation for all the parties involved."It's not a secret anymore that Abhishek Sharma is unhappy at SRH since the captaincy went to Ishan Kishan. He has been with the franchise for a long time and clearly had captaincy ambitions. Mumbai Indians, Gujarat Titans, and Punjab Kings were being explored as potential destinations, and we can't rule out Delhi Capitals either, since his mentor Yuvraj Singh is part of the set-up now," explains the source.This website reached out to SRH CEO K Shanmugam for comment, and he termed the chatter as "not true".It is further learnt that the situation has been tense since the franchise's decision to hand the captaincy to Kishan last season. It may not be a surprise if he even settles for a non-captaincy role, as the immediate priority appears to be exiting the SRH camp, a team he joined in 2019."There are not many captaincy opportunities right now. Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) and Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) are two options, but most other teams appear sorted. So even if SRH and Abhishek agree to part ways, the big question remains: where to? And how will SRH position itself even if they agree? A cash deal? Player trade? Lots of factors," adds the source.Abhishek remains the hottest property in the T20 circuit at the moment, and the World No. 2 batter will continue attracting a lot of attention in the coming weeks. While sources close to the player have maintained that "nothing is happening", the IPL ecosystem is keeping a keen eye on the developments in the SRH camp.Many factors must align for such a move to happen, and it remains to be seen whether SRH can convince one of their MVPs to stay. The move could well be delayed, but as things stand, the future of the two parties doesn't look too bright. articles.body: Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi will not attend the Asian Games gold medal match between India and Pakistan in Nisshin, Japan, on Saturday.The ACC confirmed that Naqvi will miss the final at Korogi Park because of "prior commitments". India and Pakistan will meet for the gold medal after Sri Lanka and Bangladesh play the bronze-medal match."ACC president, Mohsin Naqvi, will miss Finals Day at Asian Games 2026 due to prior commitments, but sends his very best wishes to all four teams ahead of the Gold and Bronze Medal Matches," the official media handle of ACC posted on its 'X' handle.Naqvi is the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and also Pakistan's interior minister.Indian men's and women's cricket teams have refused to receive their Asia Cup trophies from Naqvi. The teams had also expressed their support for the armed forces involved in 'Operation Sindoor', after innocent Indian civilians were killed in the Pahalgam terror attack last year."Wishing all the participants the very best ahead of gold and bronze medal matches at the Asian Games 2026. Commitments will keep me away from Nagoya. But I will be looking forward to some thrilling action," Naqvi was quoted as saying in the ACC post.The BCCI has maintained that Indian teams will not receive trophies from Naqvi. The Pakistan interior minister, meanwhile, has said that if India wants the Asia Cup trophies, they will have to collect them from him.During the 2025 men's Asia Cup and this year's women's edition, Indian teams did not accept the trophy from Naqvi.There had also been questions over what would happen if Naqvi, as the head of the continental cricket body, had to present medals at the Asian Games ceremony. articles.title: Three overs left, one wicket in hand: India A hold on for thrilling draw against Australia A
articles.summary: Yash Rathod and Shams Mulani batted for more than 36 overs in a crucial eighth-wicket partnership as India A held on for a thrilling draw against
articles.body: Yash Rathod and Shams Mulani batted for more than 36 overs in a crucial eighth-wicket partnership as India A held on for a thrilling draw against Australia A on the fourth day of the second and final four-day match in Puducherry on Friday.India A won the two-match series 1-0 after recording a 162-run victory in the opening game.Chasing 365, India A resumed the day at 28/1 and were reduced to 199/7 in 60.2 overs. They eventually reached 310/9 at stumps to secure the draw.Rathod, who scored 80 off 138 balls, and Mulani, who made 29 off 131 balls, put together an 80-run stand that lasted a little over 36 overs. They faced 16 overs of the second new ball during their partnership and kept India A in the contest.With seven overs left in the day, Australia A pacer Liam Scott, who finished with 5/37, dismissed Rathod leg before wicket. Two overs later, he removed Mulani to leave India A's last-wicket pair of Nachiket Bhute and Praful Hinge with three overs to survive.Bhute, unbeaten on 20, and Hinge, unbeaten on 0, managed to see out those three overs to complete the draw.India A also had Tushar Deshpande to thank for his earlier contribution. The night watchman scored 52 off 119 balls and helped keep Australia A from taking control of the game.Deshpande added 60 runs for the third wicket with captain Devdutt Padikkal, who scored 26, as India A reached 99/2 at lunch. They added 71 runs in the morning session for the loss of overnight batter Aayush Pandey, who made 19.India A's position became difficult in the second session when they lost five wickets to slip to 205/7 at tea.Scott dismissed Padikkal after he edged behind to Josh Philippe, who was standing up to the stumps. Deshpande then mistimed a drive against fast-medium bowler Liam Hatcher and was caught at mid-off.However, Rathod and Mulani then put together the partnership that helped India A defy the victory to Australia A.Sam Harper was named Player of the Match, while Shams Mulani was adjudged Player of the Series.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brydon Carse charged by Cricket Regulator but remains available for England
articles.summary: Brydon Carse is charged by the Cricket Regulator over an incident outside a Derby nightclub but remains available for selection by England.
articles.body:
Brydon Carse has been charged by the Cricket Regulator over an incident outside a Derby nightclub but remains available for selection by England.

Carse was arrested and then de-arrested in the early hours of 23 August. A subsequent investigation into allegations of an assault was closed by Derbyshire Police with no action taken against the 31-year-old.

On Friday, the Regulator confirmed the pace bowler has been charged with breaching the England and Wales Cricket Board's (ECB) professional conduct regulations.

"The matter will now be referred to the independent Cricket Discipline Panel for adjudication," said the Regulator. "As the process is ongoing, no further comment will be made."

Carse is alleged to have breached regulation 3.2, which states: "No participant may conduct themself in a manner, do any act or make any omission at any time which is improper or which may be prejudicial to the interests of cricket or which may bring the ECB, the game of cricket or any cricketer or group of cricketers into disrepute."

In the aftermath of the Derby controversy, Carse was dropped from the England squad to play Pakistan in the second Test at Lord's and has not been called up since. He has continued to play county cricket for Durham.

On Thursday, he was left out of the squad for the one-day tri-series in Pakistan later this month, with decisions around his inclusion understood to be taken on a tour-by-tour basis.

Responding to the Regulator's charge, an ECB statement said: "We are aware of the Cricket Regulator's decision to charge Brydon Carse. Brydon now has the opportunity to respond through the established process.

"As we do not wish to prejudge the outcome, it would not be appropriate for us to comment further."

Carse currently holds a two-year England central contract that expires in the autumn of 2027. The Regulator charge has not triggered any alteration to his England deal.

Last month, white-ball captain and Carse's close friend Harry Brook said he needed a period away from the England team.

"I'm very good mates with Carsey," Brook told BBC Sport. "I've spoken a lot with him. I think he just needs time away from the international scene.

"He's working on a few things behind the scenes and hopefully he'll be ready at some point in the future."

England are supporting Carse through the Regulator's process, though the player will be left to make his own response to the charge.

The Derby incident was another late-night drinking controversy in a year when England have been dogged by off-field problems.

As a result, Test captain Joe Root said he was "hacked off" and also addressed his team to remind them of their responsibilities.

White-ball coach Brendon McCullum said Carse would need to "get his house in order" before he returned to the England team.

And new Test coach Stephen Fleming said players will be expected to meet the "standards" of an England cricketer.

"We pick on runs and wickets primarily, but I think it's foolish not to also say there are standards that need to be set," said Fleming.

"You need to behave in accordance with your position. We're in a very privileged position, and it's understanding that privilege and what goes along with it. It can't be convenient. You can't be when it suits you to do the right things, then when you don't want it to suit you, not."

"The matter will now be referred to the independent Cricket Discipline Panel for adjudication.

"As the process is ongoing, no further comment will be made."

Regulation 3.2 states that "no participant may conduct themself in a manner, do any act or make any omission at any time which is improper or which may be prejudicial to the interests of cricket or which may bring the ECB, the game of cricket or any cricketer or group of cricketers into disrepute".

An ECB spokesperson said: "We are aware of the Cricket Regulator's decision to charge Brydon Carse. Brydon now has the opportunity to respond through the established process.

'Carse needs time away from the international scene'

"As far as Carsey is concerned, it's a good chance for him now to get his house in order and then push for selection for the next opportunity that arises."

Test captain Joe Root described himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.

On Carse, he said: "I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself."

articles.title: “Don’t Think A’ja Wilson Did Anything Wrong”: Former Pro Bowler Makes Thoughts Clear on Aces Star’s Courtside Altercation with Indiana Fan
articles.summary: A’ja Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces moved to the semifinals after beating Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever in Game 3 on Thursday, winning the first-round s...
articles.body:
A'ja Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces moved to the semifinals after beating Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever in Game 3 on Thursday, winning the first-round series 2-1. However, Wilson became involved in a controversy during Game 2 on Tuesday in Indianapolis, where she confronted a fan who pointed at her and said something after she was fouled by Sophie Cunningham.

The fan was not ejected, and the league is not punishing Wilson for the incident. People have been divided in the aftermath, with Wilson having several defenders, including former NFL star T.J. Houshmandzadeh. The former Pro Bowler defended her during the "Speakeasy" podcast, though he also said he believes the fan did nothing wrong.

"I don't think A'ja Wilson did anything wrong. I don't. I don't think the fan did anything wrong. I don't think either of them did anything wrong," he said.

During the incident, Wilson confronted the fan who was pointing at her and was yelling, "That was on you." It was more of a verbal confrontation and did not lead to anything physical, as Houshmandzadeh pointed out during the podcast. Houshmandzadeh did admit that he believed Wilson overreacted and added that she should not have doubled down after the incident.

A'Ja Wilson Has Already Put Incident With Fan in Indianapolis Behind Her

For Game 3 on Thursday, A'Ja Wilson had a double-double performance with 36 points and 10 rebounds, leading the Aces to a 94-83 win at home and moving on to the next round. She addressed the verbal altercation during Game 2 and said she has already put the incident behind her.

"I have my moments because I'm human," she said. "But after a while, I understood I didn't want that to be a distraction to myself and my team, and I knew what we had to do coming into tonight. So I put it behind me. I prayed a lot. I cried a lot."

The Aces now await the winner of the Golden State Valkyries vs. Dallas Wings series, which is currently tied at 1-1. Should they move on to the finals, they will face the winner of the Atlanta Dream vs. New York Liberty series, which has yet to begin.

articles.title: Lhuan-dre Pretorius breaks Chris Gayle's record for highest T20 score with unbeaten 188
articles.summary: Lhuan-dre Pretorius breaks Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.
articles.body:
Titans 267-3 (20 overs): Pretorius 188* (79); Boast 1-46

Knights 143 (17.2 overs): Cloete 39 (25); Ferreira 3-16

Lhuan-dre Pretorius has broken Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.

The 20-year-old South African's knock off 79 deliveries, including 13 sixes and 15 fours, helped Titans post 267-3 against Knights in the CSA T20 Challenge.

It eclipsed the 175 made by Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore (now Bengaluru) against Pune Warriors in the 2013 Indian Premier League.

Pretorius, who has played 17 T20s, three one-dayers and two Tests for South Africa, finished with a strike rate of 237.97.

He made his half-century off 24 balls but only required 16 more balls to get to three figures and then got to 150 off just 58 deliveries.

Titans then bowled out Knights for 143 to wrap up an emphatic 124-run victory at the Mangaung Oval in Bloemfontein.

articles.title: ‘A third peak’: AB de Villiers on Virat Kohli’s aggressive ODI approach ahead of 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: AB de Villiers is delighted to see his old friend and Royal Challengers Bengaluru teammate Virat Kohli flourish in ODIs, the only format in which he now
articles.body: AB de Villiers is delighted to see his old friend and Royal Challengers Bengaluru teammate Virat Kohli flourish in ODIs, the only format in which he now plays for India.In the opening ODI against West Indies at Thiruvananthapuram, Kohli smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, hitting nine sixes and 10 fours to steer India through a 296-run chase with eight wickets to spare.Asked what had changed in Kohli’s ODI game, de Villiers said, "I have been following his progress with a lot of interest and it makes me very happy to see the way he's performing, especially keeping in mind that the 2027 World Cup is just around the corner. And what stands out to me is the aggressive nature of his approach these days. It's fantastic to see him using all his experience and realizing to be positive and getting into good positions actually brings out the best in him."De Villiers, who is set to feature in WCL, which will be broadcast on FanCode, termed Kohli’s current phase his "third peak"."It's an incredible run of form. We've seen this kind of form in 2012 to 2014 and then again 2016 to 2019 and now this is a third peak for him really taking his game to the next level. And we've often heard him speak about sort of taking his game to the next level, thinking about the game a little bit differently. And you can see that in that positive and that aggressive approach he's taking on. So, it makes me very happy to see him perform like he is," de Villiers said.'Mr 360 degree' is equally excited about the ODI World Cup returning to South Africa for the first time since 2003. He hopes the Proteas can go further this time after failing to reach the semifinals in 2003 and believes their recent ODI series win over world champions Australia is an encouraging sign."I think that the cricket is going to be magnificent, as it was in 2003 and hopefully the Proteas will perform better this time than back then. From a performance point of view, it doesn't bring back great memories. But the team really looks strong now. Most of the players are still relatively unknown globally, but I know they have a lot of chemistry. There's a great (team) culture. There's lots of individuals who can win your games of cricket. And we showcased it now against Australia, winning a sixth consecutive ODI series win against the Aussies.
