articles.title: 406 chased, questions remain: Are India’s home ODI highways preparing them for 2027 World Cup?
articles.summary: Guwahati: Guwahati’s 406-run chase was a statement of India’s batting power.
articles.body: Guwahati: Guwahati’s 406-run chase was a statement of India’s batting power. Shubman Gill’s record-breaking double hundred, Rohit Sharma’s attacking start and another successful pursuit of a 400-plus target reinforced the aggressive ODI blueprint India have embraced since the 2023 World Cup.Yet the post-match comments from head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak pointed to a larger question: how much do these batting paradises prepare India for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia?Gambhir was unequivocal.“There has to be a bit more contest between bat and ball because this is not cricket, this is only batting,” he said after the match.His concern was not India’s batting but the lack of relevance such surfaces offer a bowling attack preparing for major tournaments. On a wicket where both teams crossed 400, debutant Auqib Nabi leaked 84 runs in 8.5 overs and Indian bowlers struggled for control.“You’ve got to give something to the bowlers so there’s at least something they can work with,” Gambhir said.Kotak offered a more measured perspective, stressing that India must be prepared for whatever conditions await them. “We should be preparing for whichever conditions. Our batsmen, touchwood, should be ready for any conditions,” he said.The reality probably lies somewhere between the two views.The 2027 World Cup venues are officially confirmed: eight in South Africa, three in Zimbabwe and one in Namibia. They include Johannesburg, Centurion, Cape Town, Durban, Paarl, Bloemfontein, Gqeberha and East London in South Africa.While modern South African ODI pitches are more batting-friendly than they were a decade ago, they generally offer greater pace, bounce and seam movement than the surfaces India have been playing on during this home series.But while the venues are known, precisely how the pitches will play during the tournament is not. That makes matches such as Guwahati neither irrelevant nor a direct rehearsal for the World Cup.For India’s batters, repeatedly dominating good home surfaces provides valuable practice in converting starts into big scores, sustaining an aggressive tempo and handling the pressure of chasing imposing totals. Gill’s innings also demonstrated the ability to maintain intensity after spending four hours on the field in difficult humidity.But South Africa could demand another layer of batting skill where stroke-making is not as straightforward. The ability to shift gears when conditions refuse to cooperate could prove as important as scoring at ten per over when they do.The India think tank appears conscious of that. Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule recently said the management was “very much aware” of the type of surfaces expected in South Africa and was trying to identify players who could have an impact there. He also pointed to the bounce in the Thiruvananthapuram ODI as closer to what India might encounter abroad.The bigger test over the next year, however, could be bowling.Gambhir’s comments on Auqib Nabi and Gurnoor Brar revealed a willingness to expose young bowlers to pressure situations rather than protect their statistics. “The more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said of Brar.That philosophy could become equally important with the bat. If India spend much of the next year scoring freely on home highways, they will learn how to dominate when conditions allow it. The real preparation for South Africa may come when they also experience situations where dominance is not immediately possible – like the tour of New Zealand starting in three-weeks’ time.The BCCI’s, currently announced, home calendar has three ODIs against West Indies, three against Sri Lanka and three against Zimbabwe — nine scheduled home ODIs through Jan 2027. India’s complete ODI schedule before the World Cup is not yet fixed.Guwahati proved India can chase 400. The next year must establish whether they can consistently find a way to win when anything between 280-350 is enough — and when conditions demand patience before acceleration.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India-Pakistan Asian Games final: Cricketers eye gold, but tricky pitch could level the field
articles.summary: NAGOYA: The 2,500-capacity Korogi Sports Centre is expected to be packed on Saturday, with spectators from across Japan and beyond snapping up tickets
articles.body: NAGOYA: The 2,500-capacity Korogi Sports Centre is expected to be packed on Saturday, with spectators from across Japan and beyond snapping up tickets well in advance. The India-Pakistan cricket match tends to create its own atmosphere and the Asian Games final should be no different.Striking contrast to their edge-of-the-seat meeting in the men’s hockey semifinals on Friday, when one empty seat would have been entirely at a premium although, to be fair, that venue was tucked away in the middle of nowhere.On the cricket field, the equation is far less evenly poised. India will begin as overwhelming favourites in a contest they lead 14-3 in head-to-head meetings and enter with a six-match winning streak. With the defending champions boasting greater firepower and the challenge for the latter is formidable.India brushed aside Sri Lanka in their last-four contest, winning by 124 runs. Pakistan, meanwhile, were pushed deep by Bangladesh before Abdul Samad pulled them out of trouble. Hasan Nawaz’s 27 and Salman Ali Agha’s 30 eventually took Pakistan across the line with three balls to spare.The pitch here, worryingly, could be the great leveller. The two semifinals were played on an uneven surface that offered variable bounce and plenty of turn. Apart from Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Ishan Kishan, batters from both sides struggled to find their rhythm. That makes Pakistan’s young spin duo of Arafat Minhas and Sufyan Moqim particularly interesting. How they cope with India’s formidable batting line-up could have a major bearing on the final.India has greater pedigree and deeper resources. Pakistan, though, has shown decent conditions that can narrow the gap. Unlike the recent ACC events, in which India returned without collecting the winners’ trophy from the Asian Cricket Association chief, Mohsin Naqvi, who is also Pakistan’s interior minister, the medals will be theirs to take, as he has decided to skip the event.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs West Indies in New Chandigarh: Will Siraj, Jaiswal get game time in ODI series finale?
articles.summary: NEW CHANDIGARH: After the third ODI against West Indies here on Saturday, India play another 11 ODIs this winter before they step into the World Cup year.
articles.body: NEW CHANDIGARH: After the third ODI against West Indies here on Saturday, India play another 11 ODIs this winter before they step into the World Cup year. The schedule between the IPL and their first game of the World Cup on Oct 7, 2027 hasn’t been announced yet.The team management has just started carrying out experiments to arrive at a settled core of players as per the conditions expected in South Africa. Thus, the awkward questions have popped up again. Will Yashasvi Jaiswal get a game at the top of the order? Will Mohammed Siraj be given another shot at regaining his form with the new ball?The selectors and the team management have been cold in picking players as per assignments. As for Jaiswal, they have been spending sleepless nights over giving him enough exposure as a backup opener to Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill. They managed to find him a place in the third ODI against Afghanistan in June when captain Gill decided to step down the order and bat at No.3. Like that game, Saturday’s match too is a dead rubber with India already having sealed the series 2-0.As for Siraj, it is understood the team management has lost faith in him after he struggled in the Test series in Sri Lanka in Aug. TOI understands he was conveyed he wasn’t going to get a game in the series when he joined the team before the first ODI. He has been made to go through extensive fitness routines. With Prasidh Krishna ruled out due to injury, logic dictates a senior pacer like Siraj must get a look-in unless the team management decides to go with Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar and Nitish Kumar Reddy as their seam-bowling choices.The anxiety within the team management stems from the lack of quality ODIs left before the World Cup. While condemning the pitch for the run fest in the previous game in Guwahati, head coach Gautam Gambhir subtly hinted that the six home ODIs this season — three each against Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe — can’t be considered the perfect yardstick to judge the form of players.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Lone Nasir Muzaffar produced a stunning all-round display to put Jammu & Kashmir in command on Day Two of the Irani Cup, while Rest of India pacer Mukesh
articles.body: Lone Nasir Muzaffar produced a stunning all-round display to put Jammu & Kashmir in command on Day Two of the Irani Cup, while Rest of India pacer Mukesh Choudhary answered with a five-wicket haul to keep the contest alive.Replying to RoI’s 237, J&K looked in deep trouble at 166 for eight before Muzaffar launched a remarkable counterattack. Batting at No. 10 and wearing teammate Vivrant Sharma’s jersey after being drafted in at the last moment, the 29-year-old followed his figures of 3/59 with a blazing 64 off 58 balls, hitting eight fours and three sixes.His late assault, combined with skipper Paras Dogra’s gritty 75 and Abdul Samad’s 57, powered J&K to 278 and a valuable 41-run first-innings lead. Muzaffar and Dogra added 64 runs for the ninth wicket before the tailender farmed the strike brilliantly in a rapid 48-run stand with last man Sunil Kumar.Earlier, Choudhary starred with the ball, claiming 5/78 in 19 overs.India pacer Akash Deep also impressed, taking 3/43, including the wicket of Muzaffar.By stumps, RoI were 24 for one in their second innings.Brief Scores: Rest of India 237 & 24/1. articles.title: Tharindu Ratnayake’s blazing 65 helps Sri Lanka beat Bangladesh, win Asian Games cricket bronze
articles.summary: Sri Lanka bounced back from their heavy semifinal defeat to India with a 63-run win over Bangladesh to claim the bronze medal in the men’s cricket
articles.body: Sri Lanka bounced back from their heavy semifinal defeat to India with a 63-run win over Bangladesh to claim the bronze medal in the men’s cricket tournament at the 2026 Asian Games.Playing at the Aichi Prefectural Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan, Sri Lanka were in serious trouble after being asked to bat first, slipping to 24/4 inside five overs.Ratnayake, Arachchige rescue Sri LankaTharindu Ratnayake produced a sensational counterattack to revive the innings. The lower-order batter smashed 65 off just 32 balls, hitting seven fours and five sixes, while captain Sahan Arachchige provided stability with a composed 33 off 37 deliveries.Their efforts helped Sri Lanka recover from the early collapse and post 165/9 in 20 overs, setting Bangladesh a challenging target on a difficult surface.Thushara-led attack bowls Bangladesh outBangladesh's chase got off to a disastrous start as Nuwan Thushara struck with the first ball, dismissing Litton Das for a golden duck. Bangladesh slipped to 18/4 and never recovered.Nasum Ahmed (26) and Yasir Ali (21) offered some resistance, but Sri Lanka continued to pick up wickets at regular intervals. Wanuja Sahan, Tharindu Ratnayake, Vijayakanth Viyaskanth and Nuwan Thushara claimed two wickets apiece as Bangladesh were bowled out for 102 in 17.3 overs.Sri Lanka completed a 63-run victory to secure the bronze medal, with Ratnayake's all-round performance proving decisive.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was looking in fine touch during the Asian Games 2026 final between India and Pakistan before his promising stay at the crease was cut short by Saim Ayub. However, it was Ayub’s reaction after the dismissal that quickly grabbed attention.The 15-year-old Indian opener had raced to 15 off just nine deliveries, including two sixes, as India made a brisk start after opting to bat first. But Ayub produced the breakthrough when he pushed one quicker and just outside off. Sooryavanshi attempted a reverse sweep and the ball went through to the wicketkeeper after a difficult catch, with Usman Khan eventually holding on after a couple of fumbles.As Sooryavanshi walked back, Ayub turned towards the youngster and made a pointed send-off gesture.
